title: The inequality [Gamma_B : Gamma_A] times [kappa_B : kappa_A] at most [L : K] for a finite extension of valuation rings

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite family of elements of a valued field with pairwise distinct valuations cannot sum to zero: after a minimal valuation is normalized to zero, the remaining terms have strictly larger valuation while a unit term cannot be cancelled by them
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 37353-37371, where the index set P of minimal valuation is introduced, the coefficients are normalized and the sum over P is shown to be nonzero
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the contradiction that proves the products b_i c_j are K-linearly independent.

standard_prerequisites.name: If b_1, ..., b_n are units whose residue classes in kappa_B are linearly independent over kappa_A and the coefficients a_ij are units, then the sum of the a_ij b_i over the index set P has valuation zero, hence is a unit of B
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the valuation of the partial sum over P with the valuation of the chosen minimal term, which is what makes the whole sum nonzero.

standard_prerequisites.name: Nonzero elements c_1, ..., c_m of B whose images in Gamma_B over Gamma_A are pairwise distinct force, for a fixed minimal valuation, the equality j = j_0 of the second index
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the index set P of minimal valuation to a single value of j, which is what allows the residue classes of the b_i to be used in the next step.

core_obligations: Choose witnesses for the two cardinalities: let b_1, ..., b_n in B be units whose images in kappa_B are linearly independent over kappa_A, and let c_1, ..., c_m in B be nonzero elements whose images in the quotient Gamma_B over Gamma_A are pairwise distinct; the claim of the proof is that the n times m products b_i c_j are K-linearly independent in L (proof lines 37345-37348).

Reformulate the claim as a nonvanishing statement for a linear combination with coefficients a_ij in K: a sum of a_ij b_i c_j with not all coefficients zero cannot be zero; choose an index (i_0, j_0) where the valuation v(a_ij b_i c_j) is minimal and normalize by dividing the coefficients by a_{i_0j_0}, so that a_{i_0j_0} = 1 (proof lines 37349-37355).

Define P as the set of index pairs where the valuation is exactly the minimal one, and use the choice of the c_j to conclude that (i, j) in P implies j = j_0, hence that every coefficient a_ij with (i, j) in P is a unit, as its valuation equals zero (proof lines 37356-37362).

Apply the independence of the residue classes of the b_i to see that the sum of a_ij b_i over the pairs in P is a unit of B, so that the valuation of the partial sum of a_ij b_i c_j over P equals v(c_{j_0}), which is the minimal valuation (proof lines 37362-37369).

Conclude the nonvanishing: all terms outside P have strictly larger valuation than the partial sum over P, so the full sum cannot be zero; this proves the K-linear independence of the products b_i c_j, and with it the finiteness of the residue field extension and of the index, and the inequality [Gamma_B : Gamma_A] [kappa_B : kappa_A] at most [L : K] (proof lines 37369-37373).
proof_roadmap: Pick units b_1, ..., b_n in B independent modulo the maximal ideal over kappa_A and nonzero c_1, ..., c_m in B with distinct classes in Gamma_B over Gamma_A (proof lines 37345-37347).

Assume a K-linear relation among the products b_i c_j, choose a coefficient of minimal valuation, normalize it to one and let P be the set of index pairs attaining that minimal valuation (proof lines 37349-37358).

Use distinctness of the c_j to force j = j_0 on P, then use independence of the b_i to show that the partial sum over P is a unit, while all other terms have strictly larger valuation (proof lines 37360-37371).
Conclude that no nontrivial relation exists, so that n times m is at most the degree [L : K], which is the displayed inequality (proof lines 37371-37373).
difficulty_reason: The statement controls a finite extension L over K of fraction fields of valuation rings A contained in B by the two invariants of the extension of valuation rings: it asserts that the residue field extension is finite, that the index of Gamma_A in Gamma_B is finite, and that the product of the two degrees is at most the degree of the field extension (statement lines 37333-37342). The proof is the standard construction of a K-linearly independent family of size equal to the product of the two invariants: units of B that are independent modulo the maximal ideal, and nonzero elements with distinct classes in Gamma_B over Gamma_A, are multiplied together and shown to be linearly independent by a minimal-valuation argument in which the two choices enter at different places (proof lines 37345-37371). The delicate point is that the index set of minimal valuation has to be reduced to a single value of the second index before the residue classes of the first family can be used, which is exactly why the two families are chosen in the way they are. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing, and the remark that follows the lemma at source lines 37330-37331, saying that the field extension is not required to be finite, is outside the counted spans.
